page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a memory-optimized cloud server within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration includes 512.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, and bundles 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations show high execution throughput across both single-threaded and parallel tasks, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2773.0 and a multi-core score of 28247.0. The memory subsystem sustains large-block uncached read speeds of 533.09 GB/sec and write speeds of 205.9 GB/sec. CPU instruction support covers AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration, contributing to strong software compilation results in Clang and 111.85 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

The server provides high memory density and dedicated core resources without shared-CPU contention. Because GPU accelerators are omitted, highly parallel matrix training workloads are constrained, though CPU-based inference remains viable for smaller language models. The combination of dedicated AMD cores, 512 GB of RAM, and local NVMe capacity fits in-memory caching systems, large relational databases, CI/CD compilation farms, and intensive analytics pipelines.
description: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a memory-optimized instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute line designed for resource-heavy workloads. Driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation, alongside 3840 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address. The server includes no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in top tiers for Geekbench multi-core execution, PassMark CPU tests, and software compilation via Clang. The memory subsystem sustains uncached read bandwidth exceeding 533 GB/sec, while Redis benchmarks register over 111 million operations per second. This balance of dedicated core density, extensive RAM, and rapid local storage makes the server suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caches, data analytics, and continuous integration pipelines.
